백.forms: Sino-Korean · money, large numbers (백 원, 오백, 백만)

신호등.x: Cross when the traffic light turns green.

하얗다.x: It snowed, so the streets are white.
하얗다.e: 하얀 눈 = white snow. 흰색 also means white.
하얗다.t: Note the spelling: 하얗다 → 하얘요 (with ㅒ), not 하애요.

새것.x: This phone is secondhand, but it's as clean as a new one.
새것.e: 새 'new' plus 것 'thing', written as one word.

중간고사.ex: 다음 주에 중간고사가 있어서 도서관에 가요.
중간고사.x: I have midterms next week, so I'm going to the library.
중간고사.t: Often shortened to 중간 in casual talk: 중간 끝났어요?

익다.m: to be cooked, to be done; to ripen
익다.x: When the meat is fully cooked, turn off the heat.
익다.e: Means both 'be cooked' and 'ripen'; also 'familiar', as in 낯익다 'to look familiar'.

생산하다.ex: 이 공장은 하루에 자동차를 천 대 생산해요.
생산하다.x: This factory produces a thousand cars a day.
생산하다.e: Literally 'bring to life and give birth'.

턱.x: My dad has a lot of stubble on his chin.
턱.e: Homonym warning: 턱 also means a raised ledge, as in 문턱 'doorsill.'
턱.t: 한턱내다 means to treat people to a meal, usually to celebrate good news.

경제.ex: 요즘 경제가 어려워서 다들 돈을 아껴요.
경제.x: The economy is tough these days, so everyone is saving money.
경제.e: Short for an old phrase, 'govern the world and relieve the people.'

식물.x: If you grow plants in your room, the air gets better.
식물.e: Literally 'planted thing'; its partner is 동물, 'moving thing.'
식물.t: Pronounced [싱물] — nasalization of ㄱ before ㅁ.

송별회.ex: 다음 주에 떠나는 동료의 송별회를 열었어요.
송별회.x: We threw a farewell party for a coworker leaving next week.

농사.x: My grandfather farms in the countryside.
농사.t: Use 짓다 with it: 농사를 짓다 = to farm (ㅅ irregular: 지어요).

굵다.x: Suddenly big raindrops started to fall.
굵다.e: For cylinder-like thickness (arms, rope); thick books use 두껍다.
굵다.t: Pronounced [국따]; before a vowel the ㄹ comes back: 굵어요 [굴거요].

앵커.ex: 저녁 뉴스 앵커가 오늘의 주요 소식을 전했어요.
앵커.x: The evening news anchor delivered today's top stories.
앵커.e: From English 'anchor', but only the newscaster sense; a ship's anchor is 닻.

생물.x: There are still many unknown creatures in the ocean.
생물.t: As a school subject, students say 생물 for biology, though the official course name is 생명과학.

국회.ex: 국회에서 예산을 두고 긴 토론이 이어졌습니다.
국회.x: A long debate over the budget continued in the National Assembly.
국회.t: Pronounced [구쾨] — ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes aspirated ㅋ.

걸핏하면.m: at the slightest provocation, at every turn, too readily
걸핏하면.x: My older brother gets angry at the drop of a hat.
걸핏하면.e: Built from the old verb 걸핏하다 plus -면 'if': 'whenever the slightest thing happens'.
걸핏하면.t: Pronounced [걸피타면]; used with annoying habits, much like the casual synonym 툭하면.
rel: at the drop of a hat

막연히.ex: 어릴 때는 막연히 의사가 되고 싶었어요.
막연히.x: When I was young, I vaguely wanted to become a doctor.
막연히.e: Literally 'desert-like': vast and hazy, with no clear outline.

뜻밖에.x: I unexpectedly ran into an old friend on the street.
뜻밖에.e: 뜻 'intention, expectation' + 밖에 'outside': outside of what you expected.
뜻밖에.t: Pronounced [뜯빠께]; 뜻밖의 + noun is common: 뜻밖의 소식 'unexpected news'.

혹은.forms: A 혹은 B (formal) · A 또는 B · A(이)나 B (casual)
혹은.ex: 신청서는 이메일 혹은 우편으로 보내 주세요.
혹은.x: Please send the application by email or by mail.
혹은.e: 혹 'perhaps, some' + -은; also seen in 혹시 'by any chance'.

가로막다.m: to block (the way), to obstruct, to stand in the way
가로막다.x: A big truck is blocking the alley.
가로막다.e: Built from 가로 (across, sideways) + 막다 (to block): blocking across the path.
가로막다.t: Pronounced [가로막따]; also figurative: 꿈을 가로막다 = to stand in the way of a dream.

낙선.ex: 그는 두 번 낙선한 끝에 마침내 당선되었습니다.
낙선.x: After losing twice, he was finally elected.
낙선.t: Opposite: 당선 (being elected); both often take 되다 or 하다: 낙선하다, 당선되다.

항소.x: The defendant refused to accept the ruling and appealed.
항소.t: 항소 is the first appeal; a further appeal to the Supreme Court is 상고.

인문학.ex: 요즘 직장인들 사이에서 인문학 강의가 인기가 많아요.
인문학.x: These days humanities lectures are very popular among office workers.
인문학.e: Literally 'study of human culture'. -학 = field of study: 과학, 경제학.

과대평가하다.x: Many people overestimate their own abilities.

견물생심.m: seeing something makes you want it; temptation at the sight of things
견물생심.ex: 견물생심이라고, 매장에 가면 계획에 없던 물건을 사게 돼요.
견물생심.x: Seeing is wanting, as they say—when I go to a store, I end up buying things I hadn't planned to.
견물생심.e: Literally 'see a thing, and desire arises in the heart.'

막을 내리다.forms: 막을 내려요 · 막을 내렸어요 · 막을 내릴 거예요
막을 내리다.m: to come to an end; to close (an event or era)
막을 내리다.x: The two-week festival came to a close yesterday.
막을 내리다.e: Literally 'to lower the curtain,' as at the end of a play.

징후.ex: 경기 회복의 징후가 조금씩 나타나고 있습니다.
징후.x: Signs of economic recovery are gradually appearing.

부전공.x: I'm studying Chinese as my minor.

색감.m: color sense, feel of the colors
색감.x: The colors in this painting feel really warm.

십년감수.m: being scared half to death, a close call (lit. losing ten years of one's life)
십년감수.x: A car suddenly darted out, and it scared the life out of me.
십년감수.e: Literally 'ten years cut from one's lifespan' — a fright so bad it feels like it shortened your life.
십년감수.t: Pronounced [심년감수]. Said right after a near miss: 아이고, 십년감수했네!

방조.ex: 그는 사기 범행을 방조한 혐의로 재판에 넘겨졌습니다.
방조.x: He was put on trial for aiding and abetting the fraud.
방조.e: Literally 'helping and assisting' — knowingly helping someone commit a crime.

정부실패.ex: 잘못된 규제는 정부실패를 낳을 수 있습니다.
정부실패.x: Bad regulations can lead to government failure.
정부실패.e: 정부 'government' + 실패 'failure' — when intervention makes things worse.

업보.ex: 사람들은 그의 불행을 지난 잘못의 업보라고 말했어요.
업보.x: People said his misfortune was karma for his past wrongs.
업보.e: Literally 'deeds repaid'; 업 is the Buddhist word for karma.
업보.t: In everyday talk, 자업자득 or 인과응보 are common ways to say 'you reap what you sow'.

과잉행동.x: If a child's hyperactivity is severe, consult a specialist.

처녀작.m: first work, maiden work, debut work
처녀작.ex: 그의 처녀작은 출간되자마자 큰 인기를 얻었어요.
처녀작.x: His first work became hugely popular as soon as it was published.
처녀작.e: 처녀 'maiden' + -작 'work': an author's very first published work.
처녀작.t: 데뷔작 is the more modern, neutral word for the same idea.

왕비.ex: 명성황후는 조선의 스물여섯 번째 왕 고종의 왕비였어요.
왕비.x: Empress Myeongseong was the queen of Gojong, Joseon's twenty-sixth king.
왕비.t: A queen who rules in her own right is 여왕.

국권.ex: 많은 사람들이 빼앗긴 국권을 되찾기 위해 싸웠어요.
국권.x: Many people fought to regain the nation's lost sovereignty.

낙장불입.m: no take-backs, what's done can't be undone
낙장불입.ex: 한번 낸 카드는 낙장불입이니까 다시 가져갈 수 없어요.
낙장불입.x: Once a card is played, there are no take-backs, so you can't pick it up again.
낙장불입.e: Literally 'a dropped card doesn't come back in' — a rule from the card game hwatu.
낙장불입.t: Used jokingly beyond games, meaning a decision or statement can't be reversed.

정갈하다.x: Grandma laid out a neat, carefully prepared meal for us.
정갈하다.e: A native Korean word, not built from hanja; a classic word for neat, lovingly prepared food.
정갈하다.t: Very common in food reviews: 정갈한 한정식 'a neat, carefully presented Korean set meal'.

영구동토층.ex: 영구동토층이 녹으면 메탄이 대기 중으로 나옵니다.
영구동토층.x: When permafrost thaws, methane is released into the atmosphere.

일껏.m: taking all the trouble (only to be disappointed), with great effort
일껏.ex: 일껏 음식을 준비했는데 아무도 오지 않았어요.
일껏.x: I went to all the trouble of making food, but nobody came.
일껏.e: Usually sets up a letdown: 일껏 ~했는데 = went to all that trouble, but...

자정능력.ex: 언론이 자정능력을 잃었다는 비판이 나오고 있어요.
자정능력.x: There is criticism that the press has lost its ability to correct itself.
자정능력.e: Literally 'the power to clean oneself', said of rivers and of institutions.
자정능력.t: Pronounced [자정능녁]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

각주구검.m: foolishly sticking to outdated ways, failing to adapt
각주구검.ex: 시대가 바뀌었는데 옛 방식만 고집하는 건 각주구검이에요.
각주구검.x: Insisting on old methods when times have changed is like marking the boat.
각주구검.e: A man dropped his sword from a boat, marked the boat, and searched there after landing.

웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다.forms: 웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다고 · 웃는 얼굴에 침 뱉으랴
웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다.m: it's hard to be harsh with someone who is friendly (lit. you can't spit on a smiling face)
웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다.ex: 웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다고, 웃으면서 사과하니까 화를 낼 수가 없었어요.
웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다.x: You can't spit on a smiling face: he apologized with a smile, so I couldn't get angry.
웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다.e: Literally 'you can't spit (침을 뱉다) on a face that is smiling at you'.
웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다.t: Pronounced [운는 얼구레 침 몯 밴는다]. Advice that a smile and good manners soften anger, e.g. when facing an upset customer. Also quoted as 웃는 얼굴에 침 뱉으랴.
nb: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다
말 한마디로 천 냥 빚을 갚는다
열 길 물속은 알아도 한 길 사람 속은 모른다
